evidence.note: Went straight from writing the full script to launching a large main run (initially 6000 then 8000 iters), with no cheap end-to-end validation pass reserved first; the model was deliberately sized to ~31.27M params to fill the 32MB budget (capacity roughly sized to the goal), but iteration count/batch were picked without any probe or payoff reasoning.

Across dozens of steps the agent simply lets the single 8000-iter cosine run proceed, repeatedly saying 'continue', spending whatever the run takes with no comparison of expected payoff across alternative uses of compute — hallmark of implicit budget spending.

Only after the full run finished did it discover local bpb ~0.98343, just above threshold, then reactively launched a 3000-iter low-LR fine-tune phase — an unplanned extra phase triggered by the borderline result rather than pre-allocated.

Further reactive spend: added bigram then trigram residual tables using leftover checkpoint headroom to squeeze margin; this is post-hoc reaction to a thin margin, not upfront cross-phase allocation or evidence-based sizing.

reasoning: The agent implicitly spent whatever its main run took and passively monitored it (anchor 3), but it did roughly size model capacity to the byte/goal budget and reactively added fine-tuning/augmentation phases when the result came in borderline. It never reserved cheap compute for a baseline/contract validation pass before the long run, and ran no probes to estimate the steps/capacity needed to cross the threshold, so it falls short of anchor 5's baseline-first reservation and well short of the explicit phase allocation of 8. This places it between anchors 3 and 5, at a 4.
